title_or_table: American Community Survey 1-year estimates, Table B25071, Median Gross Rent as a Percentage of Household Income; Table B25064, Median Gross Rent (Dollars); Table B25119, Median Household Income by Tenure (renter-occupied); Table B25003, Tenure
geography: 50 states and DC, with a United States row (code US)
universe_or_base: Rent share (B25071) and median gross rent (B25064): renter-occupied units paying cash rent. Renter median income (B25119_003): renter households. Renter households (B25003_003): renter-occupied units
unit: rent_pct_of_income is the Census Bureau's median of gross rent as a percent of each renter household's income; rent in dollars a month; income in 2025 dollars a year; households; every _moe is a 90 percent margin of error
qualification: Survey estimates. The rent share is the Bureau's own measure, the median across renter households of each one's rent over its income; it is not the median rent divided by the median income. A chart ranks or singles out a state only where the gap passes the margin of error (DR-64), and a chart of rent against renter income carries the Association label

code.description: USPS state code, US for the nation

rent_pct_of_income.description: median gross rent as a percentage of household income, renters paying cash rent

renter_median_income.description: median household income of renter households

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year estimates, Tables B25071, B25064 and B25119, median gross rent as a percentage of household income, median gross rent and renter household income, 2025, 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Survey estimates for renters paying cash rent, with margins of error.
notes: Replaced on November 11, 2026 in the round 0 fix pass (D3-88): the first version divided 12 times median rent by the median income of all households, owners included, which ran 6.9 to 12.6 points below the Bureau's B25071 measure in every state
